question: What does the block filter's feature design add beyond a shallow-feature learned block detector (Kohlschuetter et al. 2010 / BoilerPy3) with the training data held equal?

config.group_removal: columns of removed groups set to 0 for training (never split on); pipeline unchanged

shallow_text.description: block's own shallow text statistics: lengths, word/char ratios, capitalisation, punctuation, stop-word ratio, sentence count, link density and link count, emphasis share

neighbour_shallow.description: length and link density of the previous and next block

position.description: relative position in the page (block index, characters before/after), page size, block length relative to the page median

dom_context.description: tag of the block, depth, ancestor-tag flags (main, article, nav, footer, ...), inside the detected content root, enclosing-box statistics, same-box neighbours, sibling counts, repeated-structure counts

class_id_hash.description: hashed words of the class/id attributes of the block and up to 8 ancestors (192 buckets)

heading_context.description: distance to the previous heading, h1 seen / before first h1, hashed words of the nearest heading and of the nearest h1-h3 (2 x 96 buckets)

lexical_cues.description: fixed word lists (chrome words, call-to-action verbs, month/date patterns) and hashed first two words of the block (64 buckets)

page_relations.description: duplicate text elsewhere on the page and word overlap with title, meta description and the page's long blocks

shallow_only.note: Kohlschuetter-style set: the block's shallow text features plus those of the previous and next block (their best classifier used current, previous and next block)

shallow_plus_position.note: shallow set plus relative position and page size

shallow_plus_context.note: shallow set plus position, DOM context and heading context (no hashed class/id words, no lexical cues, no page relations)

runtime_seconds.note: fit and scoring wall-clock as recorded when each model or score file was produced; training ran 5 fits in parallel, scoring 12 worker processes

summary_text: With the rest of the pipeline unchanged, a model restricted to the 22 Kohlschuetter-style shallow features (the block's own plus the previous and next block's) scores F1 0.8435 against 0.8593 for the full 535-feature model (-0.0157 [-0.0206, -0.0113]) and lets more chrome through (without-snippet rate 0.0873 against 0.0552); with the filter alone the gap is larger (-0.0409 F1, without rate 0.390 against 0.204). Nearly all of that gap is recovered by adding position, DOM-tree and heading context while leaving out the hashed class/id words, lexical cues and page relations (shallow_plus_context: -0.0020 [-0.0047, +0.0009] F1, +0.0045 without rate), and DOM-tree context is the only group whose removal from the full model clearly lowers F1 (-0.0076 in the pipeline, -0.0253 filter only); dropping any other single group moves F1 by at most 0.0022 with intervals covering zero, though the hashed class/id words matter on forum pages (-0.0143 [-0.0255, -0.0053]). The block's own shallow text features are redundant given the rest (removing them leaves F1 unchanged, +0.0016 [-0.0005, +0.0039]), so on these pages the feature design adds a moderate 1.6 F1 points over a shallow learned detector trained on the same data, and that gain comes from structural context rather than from the large hashed vocabularies.
